I am an in-house game tester, AMA!
Do you enjoy endless hours on a half done game? Or is it just a boring way to get a paycheck like everyone else?

Hey there! I have been in the business a long time, I started out as a home beta tester then moved on to a company.

The reason I get up in the morning is because I know I am helping a company developed a better end product for their user, and that is all that matters :).

So yeah, I do enjoy endless hours on half done game, thanks for the question!
Does it pay well enough or is it just a source of beer money?
I am 19 and currently paid the min wage of £7.73 but I am full time. Providing I budget carefull I can live off of this amount after tax :)
What have you worked on, and how long have you been doing this? What other jobs have you held, and how is this different?

In the past I have worked on Little Big Planet 1, 2 & 3. I recently did Arkham Knight before it was released, I have done other projects but I signed an NDA so cannot say what the current projects are, sorry! I have been working for about 2-3 years now :) My jobs before this was a garage cashier and chef, nothing amazing :)

What is the some of the differences between being in-house compared to at home (but still paid) tester?

I always pictured in house testers having the more mundane tasks like finding environmental issues (jumping into walls for hours on end).

A main difference would be interaction, working with others in tester teams, lending each other hands to replicate bugs and write reports on them. that's in-house.

At home it's more isolated as you would imagine, also you may not have the required items to test the application (Multiple types of tablets, phones, pcs) but that depends on who employs you. :)

As for more mundane tasks, it can be, but at the same time we have to do speed-runs, compliance checks, functionality checks and test plans and MORE! :)
does your opinion or suggestions get taken into account or are you just testing the mechanics
Sometimes they are if the developer asks, otherwise we are just testers :)

Just finished "Grandma's Boy" (for the 100th time). What does "New High Score" mean?!

"Your shit's WIZEEEAK!!"

On a more serious note, does each game have it's own unique checklist? Who mocks it up? Finally, is this a shrinking market (for in-house testing), or is it growing/stable?

It really depends on our clients. When they come in they tell us what they want, 9 times out of 10 we will be given a "test plan" which has specific checks to run, but once in a blue moon we do unstructured, which is where you play as if you were an end user and spot any bugs along the way.

I assume by "Mocking up" you mean testing it? Well we are usually put into teams (varies) and we have a team lead, he dishes out the builds, devices and test plans.

The company I work for has soared in profit recently, we had a huge amount of clients in so we were frantically rushing around trying to get everything sorted haha. I would say it is still stable if not growing :)
Is there a weird vibe between developers and testers? I always remember that made the job so much less pleasant.

We do get the odd developer who believes we are out to make their game look like shit, which in essence IS part of the job.

I can recall once where I entered a new bug into the database and because I spelt a single word wrong he felt that my skills as a tester were hindered and should be taken off the team. But we do get the nice guys and gals too :)
